Australians hunting bargains on comparison websites risk being duped by sites that only offer a selection of preferred providers. The corporate watchdog has issued a warning after launching multiple court actions against websites for allegedly misleading consumers about the range of financial services and products on offer and, in some cases, promoting multiple leads from a single brand. While comparison websites are a good place to start for prices and services information, consumers should conduct deeper research, Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) commissioner Alan Kirkland said. "The products that are listed by many comparison sites are selected and ordered based on what the product providers pay to the comparison sites, and they may not give you a full view of the market," Mr Kirkland said. " It's important to actually use a range of comparison sites in order to get a fuller view of the market. " The Federal Court recently found comparison site Choosi — which offers life, funeral, income protection and health insurance products — misled consumers over four years from mid-2019 after claiming to compare a slew of funeral and life insurance policies, when Hannover Life Re issued all but one of the policies offered. Every single policy in question was distributed by Greenstone Financial Services, a company linked with Choosi. reason: ASIC's warning assumes comparison sites harm consumers, but the real problem may be consumer behaviour and inadequate financial literacy rather than site design.
angle: Regulator should mandate disclosure of ranking methodology rather than warn consumers away from useful tools.
